messages.content: Calculate the probability of getting a head when flipping a coin.

function.name: get_standard_deviation
function.description: Calculates the standard deviation of a series of numbers. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

population.description: A boolean indicating whether to calculate the population (true) or sample (false) standard deviation.

message.content:
For a fair (unbiased) coin, the probability of landing on heads in a single flip is

\[
P(\text{heads}) = \frac{\text{number of favorable outcomes}}{\text{total possible outcomes}} = \frac{1}{2} = 0.5 \; (\text{or } 50\%).
\]

If the coin were biased, you would need the bias value (e.g., \(p\) for heads and \(1-p\) for tails). But with no bias specified, the standard assumption is a fair coin, giving a 50 % chance of heads.
